rationale: The buyer is identifiable — software engineers with SaaS tool budgets — and the willingness-to-pay signal is direct ('I would pay on day one'), but this is a single HN comment with no corroborating volume. The decisive problem is buildability and autonomy: an AI-native source control system requires custom VCS infrastructure, multi-agent diff semantics, and a GitHub-competitive feature surface that is entirely outside what a Claude prompt + landing page + Stripe link can produce; this is a multi-engineer, multi-year infrastructure product. It cannot be built or run by this factory. Score sits below the validate threshold.
solution_plan: This opportunity is not viable for a solo non-technical operator using the Claude factory. Building a credible GitHub alternative — even an AI-native one — requires deep distributed systems engineering, custom Git protocol work, and a team. No path exists here that doesn't require a large technical co-founder and significant capital. The honest recommendation is to watch this space for a narrower wedge (e.g. an AI-native code-review workflow layer on top of existing Git) rather than attempt the full product.
notes: Fails build_gates on operational_autonomy (2 < 7) and buildability_with_ai (2 < 6). Product is fundamentally a multi-year infrastructure engineering effort, not a factory-buildable micro-service.
